facts.text: Geralt's invocation of the Law of Surprise at the feast in Cintra unknowingly bound his fate to the unborn Ciri.
As a Witcher, Geralt is sterile due to his mutations, making the idea of having a child deeply ironic to him.
For six years after the feast in Cintra, Geralt avoided returning to see Ciri, taking contracts in distant lands to escape the responsibility.
The Law of Surprise is depicted as a supernatural contract that the universe enforces with absolute rigidity in the Witcher world.
Ciri carries the Elder Blood, a genetic trait tied to prophecy and immense magical power.
Geralt's survival of the experimental mutations at Kaer Morhen is linked to his destined role as Ciri's protector.
Following the fall of Cintra, Ciri became a war refugee wandering the northern kingdoms alone.
Geralt and Ciri were reunited in Sodden after Geralt saved a merchant named Jurgen from monsters and invoked the Law of Surprise again.
Jurgen's wife had taken in an orphaned war refugee who turned out to be Ciri, leading to her reunion with Geralt.
After reuniting with Ciri, Geralt chose to accept his role as her father, abandoning his belief that he was incapable of love.
Geralt decided to take Ciri to Kaer Morhen, the mountain fortress of the Wolf School, believing it was the safest place for her.
Bringing Ciri to Kaer Morhen broke Witcher tradition, since the fortress had only ever housed Witcher recruits and trainers.
During the journey to Kaer Morhen, Geralt trained Ciri in survival skills such as hiding her trail, sleeping outdoors, and reading forest signs.
At Kaer Morhen, Ciri was cared for by Geralt's fellow Witchers Vesemir, Eskel, and Lambert, who acted as father figures and uncles to her.
Geralt personally supervised Ciri's Witcher training in swordplay and combat techniques at Kaer Morhen.
The winter Geralt and Ciri spent at Kaer Morhen became a formative period of peace that solidified their father-daughter bond.
The Rivian Pogrom occurred in the year 1268, when a tavern argument in Rivia escalated into a genocidal riot against non-humans.
Geralt was killed during the Rivian Pogrom when a terrified young man named Rob stabbed him with a pitchfork while he defended his dwarven and elven friends.
Yennefer arrived after Geralt's death in Rivia and exhausted her own life force trying to heal him, collapsing over his body.
Ciri used her Elder Blood power to transport the bodies of Geralt and Yennefer to the mystical isle of Avallon, a place outside of time, to heal them.
While Geralt and Yennefer were in limbo on Avallon, the Wild Hunt, led by Eredin, tracked Ciri's magical resonance to the island.
The Wild Hunt captured Yennefer on Avallon, intending to use her as bait to lure Ciri out of hiding.
Geralt traded his own soul to the Wild Hunt in exchange for Yennefer's freedom.
Geralt spent roughly a year serving as one of the spectral red riders of the Wild Hunt, an experience that stripped away his identity and memory.
Geralt was eventually found near Kaer Morhen with total amnesia, remembering nothing of his past, loves, or daughter.
Geralt's amnesia after the Wild Hunt ordeal serves as the foundational mystery driving the events of the first Witcher game.
Despite losing his memories, Geralt retained his combat skills and ability to cast Witcher Signs.
Letho of Gulet is a member of the largely extinct School of the Viper, known for combining brute strength with a sharp tactical mind.
Letho of Gulet made a bargain with the Emperor of Nilfgard to destabilize the northern kingdoms in exchange for restoring the Viper school.
Years before the games, Geralt saved Letho of Gulet's life from a manticore, creating a bond of debt and respect between them.
While Geralt served the Wild Hunt, Letho of Gulet and two other Viper witchers protected the amnesiac Yennefer within Nilfgardian territory.
Letho of Gulet, acting on orders from the White Flame, assassinated King Demavend of Aedirn and King Foltest of Temeria to destabilize the north.
Letho of Gulet used the Lodge of Sorceresses as a scapegoat to cover his role in the regicides.
At the end of the second Witcher game, Geralt confronts Letho of Gulet, who calmly explains his motives without asking for forgiveness.
The player can choose whether to kill or spare Letho of Gulet after learning of his role in the regicides.
The summit at Loc Muinne was held in the ruins of an ancient elven city to address the regicides and reestablish the Conclave of Mages.
The summit at Loc Muinne collapsed into violence when the Lodge of Sorceresses' plot to create a puppet state in the Pontar Valley, ruled by a dragon in human form, was exposed.
Philippa Eilhart and Sile de Tansarville were sorceresses who conspired to manipulate the political landscape at Loc Muinne.
At Loc Muinne, Geralt fully recovered his lost memories, including the events of Avallon, the Rivian Pogrom, and his bargain with Eredin.
After recovering his memories at Loc Muinne, Geralt learned that Yennefer was alive and held captive in Nilfgard, and that Ciri had returned to the world.
The collapse of the Loc Muinne summit triggered the start of the Third Northern War.
Radovid the Stern emerged as the harshest northern leader, persecuting anyone associated with magic under the guise of protecting the realm.
At the start of the Third Witcher game, Geralt arrives in White Orchard, a village devastated by the Third Northern War and Nilfgardian occupation.
In White Orchard, Geralt is accompanied by his mentor Vesemir while searching for leads on Yennefer and Ciri.
To gain information from the Nilfgardian commander in White Orchard, Geralt was forced to kill a griffin threatening supply lines.
White Orchard exposes Geralt to the cold, bureaucratic style of Nilfgardian occupation compared to the chaotic cruelty of northern lords.
Geralt's search for Ciri in The Witcher 3 leads him through three major regions: Velen, Novigrad, and Skellige.
In Velen, Geralt found evidence that Ciri had been a refugee fleeing something more dangerous than the Nilfgardian army.
In Novigrad, Geralt tracked Ciri's movements through the criminal underworld and religious authorities, finding she had matured into a resourceful, powerful woman.
In Skellige, Geralt found evidence of a magical explosion and battle linked to Ciri's flight from the Wild Hunt.
Geralt met with Emperor Emhyr var Emreis, the White Flame, in occupied Vizima, who hired him to find Ciri.
Emhyr var Emreis wanted Ciri found in order to secure an heir carrying the Elder Blood to strengthen Nilfgardian dynastic rule.
Geralt accepted Emhyr var Emreis's commission for pragmatic reasons, using imperial resources to find Ciri while intending to protect her autonomy.
Yennefer allied herself with the Nilfgardian Empire's intelligence network to help locate Ciri.
In Velen, Geralt encountered Philip Strenger, known as the Bloody Baron, who offered information on Ciri in exchange for help finding his missing wife and daughter.
The Crones of Crookback Bog, named Brewess, Weavess, and Whispess, are ancient malevolent entities who once hosted Ciri and later tried to consume her for her blood's power.
The Crones of Crookback Bog demanded blood and obedience from local peasants in exchange for protection.
Geralt performed a ritual on the Botchling, the cursed spirit of the Bloody Baron's unborn child, choosing to either destroy it or transform it into a guardian spirit called a Lubokin.
The Bloody Baron's questline in Velen serves as a mirror for Geralt's own fears about fatherhood and failing to protect Ciri.
After Velen, Geralt's search for Ciri continued in Novigrad, a city that had become gripped by religious paranoia and persecution under the Eternal Fire.
